title: Serial blood volume estimation in rabbits using trivalent chromium – An exploratory study
author: Baby, Kumar, et al.
materials: All the animal experimental protocol were approved by the institutional animal ethics committee (IAEC/KMC/07/2007–2008). New Zealand white rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus), (n = 31; male n = 10, female n = 21), over two months of age with average weight of 2.21 kg were used for the study. All rabbits were provided with 12:12 h light-dark cycle, with 28 ℃ temperature and relative humidity between 30–70% in the animal housing. Two rabbits of the same sex were hygienically housed in a stainless steel cage and the collection pans were cleaned daily with water. Rabbits were fed with food and water adlibitum, except during the experiment.

The detailed methodology for BV measurement using trivalent chromium and cannulation of rabbit ear has been described in earlier reports [4,5]. Two intravenous (IV) cannulae, of size 24 and 26 GA (BD Neoflon TM Singapore) were inserted, one on each ear, for drug injection and blood collection. 2 mCi of 51Cr in aqueous solution (CR2) was obtained from BRIT, DAE, GOI. Two syringes were loaded with 1 ml each of solution containing 51Cr and freshly prepared ascorbic acid (Sisco, India) (mass concentration of ascorbic acid =2 mg/ml), which were given holding time of two hours to ensure complete reduction of chromium to its trivalent form [6]. Activities of the loaded syringes were determined in a calibrated nucleonix gamma ray spectrometer having sodium iodide doped with thallium [NaI (TI)] based well type scintillation detector coupled to a single channel analyzer. All the activities were counted for 30 s and further converted as cps for calculations. Approximately 3000 cps of 51Cr (III) in 1 ml were injected through the IV cannula inserted into the rabbits’ right ear marginal vein, followed by 0.5 ml saline, to flush the injected 51Cr (III) solution into circulation. The syringe used for injection of the dose was measured for any activity remaining. The actual dose that was in effect administered was derived by subtracting the left-over activity in the syringe. An electronic timer was pre-set for a minute before the experiment and switched on immediately after injection. After a minute, 1 ml whole blood was obtained through the IV cannula, inserted into the rabbits’ left ear central artery and its activity was determined for 360 s. BV was calculated using the formula,BVmlV2=C1V1C2Where, Cl = cps/ml injected
C2 = cps/ml in the diluted blood

After initial measurement of BV using 51Cr (III), a repeat measurement was done exactly after sixty minutes, using the same technique as discussed above. An electronic timer was pre-set for sixty minutes and switched on immediately after the initial measurement using 51Cr (III). Two minutes before the completion of sixty minutes, 1 ml whole blood was obtained by a syringe through the IV cannula inserted into the left ear for measuring the background activity in the blood. At 60 min, approximately 3150 cps of 51Cr (III) was injected through the same IV cannula inserted in the right ear marginal vein, followed by 0.5 ml of saline to flush the injected solution into circulation. One minute later, 1 ml blood sample was obtained after dilution for repeat estimation of BV. The background sample, syringe used for injection of 51Cr (III) and the blood sample obtained after dilution was counted by the well counter for 360 s. The counts obtained from the syringe used for injection were subtracted to find the actual, activity introduced into the rabbit. Similarly, the counts obtained from the background sample were subtracted from the blood sample obtained after dilution. BV was obtained from the equation as mentioned above. The results obtained were compared with the BV measured by the initial 51Cr (III) measurement.

steps.title: Prepare animal housing conditions
steps.instruction: House New Zealand white rabbits (31 total; 10 male, 21 female) >2 months old, average weight 2.21 kg, in a 12:12 h light‑dark cycle at 28 °C and 30–70 % relative humidity; keep two same‑sex rabbits per stainless‑steel cage, clean collection pans daily with water, provide food and water ad libitum except during the experiment.

steps.title: Cannulate rabbit ears with IV catheters
steps.instruction: Insert two intravenous cannulae (BD Neoflon™, Singapore; sizes 24 GA and 26 GA) – one into the right ear marginal vein for injection and the other into the left ear central artery for blood collection.

steps.title: Prepare 51Cr tracer solution
steps.instruction: Obtain 2 mCi of 51Cr in aqueous solution (CR2) from BRIT, DAE, GOI. Load two syringes with 1 ml each of the 51Cr solution mixed with freshly prepared ascorbic acid (Sisco, India) at a mass concentration of 2 mg/ml. Hold the syringes for 2 h to ensure complete reduction of chromium to the trivalent form.

steps.title: Measure tracer activity with gamma spectrometer
steps.instruction: Determine the activity of each loaded syringe using a calibrated Nucleonix gamma‑ray spectrometer equipped with a NaI(Tl) well‑type scintillation detector coupled to a single‑channel analyzer; count each syringe for 30 s and record counts per second (cps).

steps.title: Inject tracer and flush with saline
steps.instruction: Inject approximately 3000 cps of 51Cr(III) in 1 ml through the right‑ear cannula, then immediately flush with 0.5 ml sterile saline. Measure any residual activity in the syringe; subtract this from the pre‑injection activity to obtain the actual administered dose.

steps.title: Collect first blood sample and count activity
steps.instruction: Start an electronic timer set for 1 min immediately after injection. After 1 min, withdraw 1 ml whole blood via the left‑ear cannula, place the sample in a counting tube, and count its activity for 360 s on the same well counter.

steps.title: Calculate initial blood volume
steps.instruction: Compute blood volume (BV) using the formula BV = (C1 × V1) / C2, where C1 is cps/ml of injected tracer (derived from the corrected dose), V1 is the volume of tracer injected (1 ml), and C2 is cps/ml measured in the diluted blood sample.

steps.title: Collect background sample before 60‑min repeat
steps.instruction: Two minutes before the 60‑min mark, draw 1 ml whole blood via the left‑ear cannula for background activity measurement; count this sample for 360 s.

steps.title: Inject repeat tracer dose and flush
steps.instruction: At exactly 60 min, inject approximately 3150 cps of 51Cr(III) in 1 ml through the right‑ear cannula, followed by 0.5 ml saline flush. Measure residual activity in the injection syringe and subtract it from the pre‑injection activity to obtain the actual dose for the repeat measurement.

steps.title: Collect repeat blood sample and count activity
steps.instruction: One minute after the repeat injection, withdraw 1 ml blood (after dilution) via the left‑ear cannula; also retain the syringe used for injection. Count the syringe, the background blood sample, and the repeat blood sample each for 360 s. Subtract syringe residual activity from the injected dose and subtract background counts from the repeat blood counts.

steps.title: Calculate repeat blood volume
steps.instruction: Apply the same BV = (C1 × V1) / C2 equation using the corrected repeat dose (C1) and the background‑adjusted repeat blood cps (C2) to obtain the 60‑min blood‑volume measurement.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis of measurements
steps.instruction: Analyze initial and repeat BV values with a paired t‑test and Bland‑Altman plot (using SPSS 15.0); report results as mean ± SD, consider P < 0.05 significant.
